3. Delete the unused function and its IAM execution role.
Code.Terraform: # Remove unused aws_lambda_function resource from Terraform configuration

Recommendation.Text: Delete unused Lambda functions and remove their associated IAM execution roles to reduce code storage and security footprint.

eni_detached_unused.CheckTitle: Elastic Network Interface is attached to an instance or AWS service
eni_detached_unused.Description: **Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs)** in the `available` (detached) state consume subnet IP addresses and may hold billable public IPv4 addresses.
eni_detached_unused.Risk: Orphaned ENIs exhaust VPC subnet IP space, hold security group references blocking cleanup, and can incur public IPv4 charges.

Code.NativeIaC: # Remove orphaned AWS::EC2::NetworkInterface resource
Code.Other:
1. Open Amazon EC2 console > Network Interfaces.
2. Filter by Status = available.
3. Delete detached network interfaces.
Code.Terraform: # Remove unused aws_network_interface resource from Terraform configuration

Recommendation.Text: Delete detached Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) to reclaim VPC subnet IPs and eliminate unattached IPv4 costs.

cloudformation_stack_failed_or_abandoned.CheckTitle: CloudFormation stack is not in a failed or rollback-complete state
cloudformation_stack_failed_or_abandoned.Description: **AWS CloudFormation stacks** stuck in `ROLLBACK_COMPLETE`, `CREATE_FAILED`, `DELETE_FAILED`, or `UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED` represent failed deployments that may leave partial billable resources behind.
cloudformation_stack_failed_or_abandoned.Risk: Failed or abandoned CloudFormation stacks cause infrastructure drift, consume stack quotas, and can retain orphaned billable resources.

Code.NativeIaC: # Fix template errors and redeploy or delete the failed CloudFormation stack
Code.Other:
1. Open AWS CloudFormation console > Stacks.
2. Inspect failed stacks and delete stacks in ROLLBACK_COMPLETE or DELETE_FAILED state.
Code.Terraform: # Manage stack lifecycle or migrate orphaned resources into clean IaC state

Recommendation.Text: Delete CloudFormation stacks stuck in ROLLBACK_COMPLETE or failed states and clean up any retained resources.

dynamodb_provisioned_capacity_unused.CheckTitle: DynamoDB table with provisioned capacity is actively storing items or uses On-Demand billing
dynamodb_provisioned_capacity_unused.Description: **Amazon DynamoDB tables** configured with `PROVISIONED` read/write capacity units (RCU/WCU) but containing 0 items incur continuous hourly capacity charges.
dynamodb_provisioned_capacity_unused.Risk: Empty DynamoDB tables with provisioned throughput waste monthly database budget for unused RCU and WCU reservations.

Code.NativeIaC:
Resources:
  Table:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
Code.Other:
1. Open Amazon DynamoDB console > Tables.
2. Switch empty or sporadic tables to On-Demand (PAY_PER_REQUEST) capacity mode, or delete unused tables.

Recommendation.Text: Delete unused DynamoDB tables or switch billing mode from PROVISIONED to PAY_PER_REQUEST (On-Demand).

redshift_cluster_idle.CheckTitle: Redshift cluster has active database connections
redshift_cluster_idle.Description: **Amazon Redshift clusters** with 0 database connections over 30 days incur significant multi-node data warehouse compute charges.
redshift_cluster_idle.Risk: Idle Redshift clusters generate high continuous hourly costs across all provisioned data warehouse nodes.

Code.NativeIaC: # Pause or delete idle AWS::Redshift::Cluster resources
Code.Other:
1. Open Amazon Redshift console > Clusters.
2. Pause the idle cluster or take a final snapshot and delete it.
Code.Terraform: # Remove or pause idle aws_redshift_cluster resources

Recommendation.Text: Pause or take a final snapshot and delete idle Amazon Redshift clusters with 0 connections over 30 days, or migrate to Redshift Serverless.

cloudfront_distribution_unused.Description: **Amazon CloudFront distributions** with 0 requests over 30 days represent abandoned CDN endpoints that may point to stale origins.
cloudfront_distribution_unused.Risk: Unused CloudFront distributions increase management overhead and risk subdomain takeover if origin S3 buckets or DNS targets are decommissioned.

Code.NativeIaC: # Remove unused AWS::CloudFront::Distribution resource
Code.Other:
1. Open Amazon CloudFront console.
2. Disable the unused distribution, wait for deployment, and delete it.
Code.Terraform: # Remove unused aws_cloudfront_distribution resource from Terraform configuration

Recommendation.Text: Disable and delete unused CloudFront distributions with 0 requests over 30 days and remove associated DNS records.

s3_bucket_lifecycle_missing.CheckTitle: S3 bucket has a lifecycle configuration to transition or expire objects
s3_bucket_lifecycle_missing.Description: **Amazon S3 buckets** without a lifecycle configuration retain objects in `STANDARD` storage indefinitely and never abort incomplete multipart uploads.
s3_bucket_lifecycle_missing.Risk: Missing S3 lifecycle rules lead to unbounded storage growth, orphaned incomplete multipart uploads, and higher storage tier costs.

Code.NativeIaC:
Resources:
  Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      LifecycleConfiguration:
        Rules:
          - Id: AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload
            Status: Enabled
            AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload:
              DaysAfterInitiation: 7
Code.Other:
1. Open Amazon S3 console > Buckets > Management tab.
2. Create a lifecycle rule to transition aged objects to S3 Intelligent-Tiering/Glacier and abort incomplete multipart uploads.

Recommendation.Text: Configure S3 Lifecycle rules to transition cold objects to lower-cost tiers and abort incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days.

cost_explorer_spend_tracked.CheckTitle: AWS Cost Explorer service spend is tracked and monitored
cost_explorer_spend_tracked.Description: **AWS Cost Explorer** aggregates service-level unblended costs over the evaluation period to provide visibility into top cloud spend drivers.
cost_explorer_spend_tracked.Risk: Lack of continuous service spend visibility delays detection of cost anomalies and runaway resource consumption.

Code.CLI: aws ce get-cost-and-usage --time-period Start=<START_DATE>,End=<END_DATE> --granularity MONTHLY --metrics UnblendedCost --group-by Type=DIMENSION,Key=SERVICE
Code.NativeIaC:
Resources:
  CostAnomalyMonitor:
    Type: AWS::CE::AnomalyMonitor
    Properties:
      MonitorName: ServiceMonitor
      MonitorType: DIMENSIONAL
      MonitorDimension: SERVICE
Code.Other:
1. Open AWS Cost Management console > Cost Explorer.
2. Configure AWS Budgets and Cost Anomaly Detection alerts.

Recommendation.Text: Monitor service-level spend via AWS Cost Explorer and configure AWS Budgets and Cost Anomaly Detection.

ecr_image_untagged_or_stale.CheckTitle: ECR repository does not retain untagged or stale container images without a lifecycle policy
ecr_image_untagged_or_stale.Description: **Amazon ECR repositories** without a lifecycle policy that accumulate untagged or stale container images incur ongoing ECR storage costs.
ecr_image_untagged_or_stale.Risk: Retaining untagged and obsolete container images inflates ECR storage bills and keeps vulnerable old image layers available for deployment.

Code.NativeIaC:
Resources:
  Repo:
    Type: AWS::ECR::Repository
    Properties:
      LifecyclePolicy:
        LifecyclePolicyText: |
          {"rules":[{"rulePriority":1,"selection":{"tagStatus":"untagged","countType":"sinceImagePushed","countUnit":"days","countNumber":14},"action":{"type":"expire"}}]}
Code.Other:
1. Open Amazon ECR console > Repositories.
2. Configure a Lifecycle Policy to expire untagged images after 14 days and stale images beyond retention.

Recommendation.Text: Configure an ECR Lifecycle Policy to automatically expire untagged and stale container images.

ecs_service_idle.CheckTitle: ECS service tasks are actively utilized and right-sized
ecs_service_idle.Description: **Amazon ECS services** running tasks with sustained maximum CPU and memory utilization below 5% over 30 days represent idle or over-provisioned container capacity.
ecs_service_idle.Risk: Idle or oversized ECS Fargate/EC2 services waste container compute and memory reservations continuously.

Code.NativeIaC:
Resources:
  TaskDef:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    Properties:
      Cpu: "256"
      Memory: "512"
Code.Other:
1. Open Amazon ECS console > Clusters > Services.
2. Scale down idle services to desiredCount = 0 or reduce task CPU/memory reservations.

Recommendation.Text: Scale down unused ECS services or right-size task CPU and memory reservations using Application Auto Scaling.

iam_role_unused.CheckTitle: IAM role has been used within the last 90 days
iam_role_unused.Description: **AWS IAM roles** that have not been assumed for more than 90 days (or were created over 90 days ago and never used) represent dormant privileges.
iam_role_unused.Risk: Dormant IAM roles expand the identity attack surface and can be abused for lateral movement or privilege escalation if compromised.

Code.NativeIaC: # Remove unused AWS::IAM::Role resource from CloudFormation template
Code.Other:
1. Open AWS IAM console > Roles.
2. Sort by Last activity and verify roles unused for 90+ days.
3. Detach policies and delete unused IAM roles.
Code.Terraform: # Remove unused aws_iam_role resource from Terraform configuration

Recommendation.Text: Review and delete IAM roles that have not been assumed in the last 90 days to maintain least privilege.

awslambda_function_execution_role_least_.CheckTitle: Lambda function execution role adheres to least privilege without administrative permissions
awslambda_function_execution_role_least_.Description: **AWS Lambda execution roles** should not have `AdministratorAccess` or inline policies granting wildcard `Resource: "*"` permissions.
awslambda_function_execution_role_least_.Risk: Overly permissive Lambda execution roles allow an attacker who compromises function code or dependencies to take over the AWS account.

Code.NativeIaC:
Resources:
  LambdaRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
